newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia dlr puts brave face on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia dlr puts brave face on rate worries.

text.p: The Australian dollar finished with broad based gains Friday as an upbeat performance on the crosses left it comfortably above the week's US$0.7855 low.

The initial upward impetus came from a sharp cut in Swiss interest rates which made higher yielding currencies look all the more attractive, and the momentum was sustained for a while by buying for an A$-linked dual currency samurai bond.

But the bulls were given pause by a late Japanese newswire report the bank of Japan was concerned that long-term rates there were falling too far and by loose talk the Reserve Bank might be cutting Australian rates as early as next week.
By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the local dollar had settled at US$0.7924/29 from an early US$0.7920/25 and US$0.7916/21 late here Thursday.

Analysts said a break of last week's US$0.7945 peak was needed to cement the recovery from Tuesday's US$0.7855 low and establish a solid chart base for a re-test of the September US$0.8021 high. Support had shifted up to US$0.7915 and it would take a breach of US$0.7855 to reverse the current upward bias.
On the crosses, the currency made a lot of early capital out of a 0.50 point cut in Swiss interest rates to just 1.00 percent which benefited high yielders of all colours and creeds.
The dollar was also aided by demand linked to a 30 billion yen dual currency samurai bond from the Queensland Treasury Corp, which enlivened an otherwise dull week for such issues.

But gains were pared by a burst of profit taking following the report of BOJ unease over falling Japanese bond yields. That saw it back to 87.68/78 yen from a 87.90 high, although it was still up on Thursday's 87.44/54 and 86.88 this time last week.

It was sharply up on the Swiss franc at 0.9932/46 -- its highest local close in 11 weeks -- from 0.9806/30 late Thursday, and at 1.2063/76 marks from 1.2001/16. In trade weighted terms the dollar inched up to 58.4 from 58.3.
Traders said the gains would likely have been greater had it not been for an undercurrent of unease over interest rates.

So wound up has the market become about the risk of a cut in official rates that the dollar slipped this morning when the Reserve Bank routinely cleared the wire service pages it uses to announce such events.

"No way would the RBA move on rates the Friday before its board meeting; where's the sense in that?" said one. "But that didn't stop some from raising the alarm when the bank's page cleared this morning." He expected the market to be glued to the page at 9.30 am next week, the usual time for a rate change.
Today's domestic data offered little clue to RBA intentions.

New motor vehicle registrations rose 6.9 percent in August beating median forecasts of a 3.9 percent gain. That was firm on the face of its but analysts emphasised the figures were notoriously volatile -- registrations leapt 18.5 percent in June only to plunge 17.7 percent in July.

Offshore sentiment was given a modest filip when Moody's said it might upgrade the debt of two Australian states. That followed Standard and Poor's decision to put Australia on positive creditwatch and analysts thought it only a matter of time before Moody's did the same. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
